description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Collins Aerospace develops aerospace and defense technologies, including connected aviation communication systems. The Software Engineer I will support the engineering and development of software and systems for the GLOBALink communications system, participating in design, development, testing, integration, deployment, and operational support. The role collaborates with engineering, acceptance, field operations, and international aviation stakeholders in an onsite team environment.
Software Engineer developing and integrating aviation communication systems, protocols, and high-availability network infrastructure

Responsibilities:
• The Software Engineering Intern will participate in the engineering and development of systems and software for the GLOBALink communications system utilized in worldwide aviation communications
• Development of GLOBALink products entails customer requirements elicitation, system design, software design, development, followed by unit and integration testing, and finally formal acceptance testing
• The successful intern candidate will participate in a team environment across the aforementioned engineering processes/procedures to ensure successful product development utilizing standard waterfall development in a CMMI level 3 organization
• You will perform full life-cycle software development including designing software solutions; supporting implementation, integration, acceptance testing and deployment
• You will contribute to highly technical software engineering teams on challenging software upgrades and features
• You will provide analysis for the decomposition of technical system level requirements into sub-system software requirements and design
• You will support a large-scale global aviation network infrastructure with heavy design focus in redundancy, high availability, and security
• You will develop software for air-ground/ground-ground communication, positional data processing, transport/routing/link layer protocols, and remote deployment capabilities
• You will collaborate closely with system engineering/performance, network engineering, system acceptance and field operation teams
• You will provide support for product deployment, field monitoring, troubleshooting and operator trainings
• You will participate in lab/field integration, Air Navigation Service Providers (ANSPs) from domestic US, South America, Europe and Asia
• You will utilize a mature ISO/SEI CMMI compliant process to produce all work products
• You will support project leadership, project planning, execution, monitoring and closure activities
• You will be working collaboratively onsite in our Annapolis, MD facility

Requirements:
• U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are authorized to access information under this program/contract
• Bachelor's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) major obtained by start date

Preferred:
• Knowledge of the commercial aviation industry
• Linux, Network Protocols, High Availability and Security
• The ideal candidate will have experience using disciplined development processes in a team environment
• Aerospace knowledge and experience
• Proven communication and collaboration skills to work across internal and external customers (government and commercial)
• Prior RTX internship, co-op, or work experience
